```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Purpose: 
Visualization of the necessary data taken from the raw data sets. Utilizing plots and graphs. 

## Required:
Imported data from 11_DataCleaning.Rmd file.


## Viewing the SCF data set:
```{r}

## Boxplot showing the average household income per race divided into four categories: White non-Hispanic, Black non-Hispanic, Hispanic, Other

boxplot(scf_mean$Before_Tax_Income ~ scf_mean$Category, xlab = "Race", ylab = "Before Tax Income (in Thousands USD)", main = "Before Tax Income vs Race (1989-2025)", col = c("lightblue1", "maroon1", "yellow","lightgreen" ))

```


## Viewing the DFA data set:
```{r}

## Initial boxplot showing overall net worth per race divided into four categories: White, Black, Hispanic, Other

boxplot(dfa_levels$`Net worth` ~ dfa_levels$Category, xlab = "Race", ylab = "Total Net Worth (USD)", main = "Total Net Worth vs Race (1989-2026)",col = c("lightblue1", "maroon1", "yellow","lightgreen"))

## New boxplot with Total Net Worth in thousands USD

net_worth_thousands <- dfa_levels$`Net worth` / 1000

boxplot(net_worth_thousands ~ dfa_levels$Category, xlab = "Race", ylab = "Total Net Worth (in Thousands USD)", main = "Total Net Worth vs Race (1989-2026)",col = c("lightblue1", "maroon1", "yellow","lightgreen"))

```


## Analysis:
As seen in both boxplots above, the average income per race is consistent throughout the 13-14 examined years. People who identified as White, non-Hispanic, or simply White, constantly earned more than other races. This information is sufficient to prove there is a racial weath gap in the United States of America
